title: Studio look and feel: one component library, one standard, page by page
summary: Owner direction of 24 November 2026: rework the confusing Access page, turn its lessons into standards, then rework every page step by step with owner review, using standard components developed as an area of their own. Counted at develop 1b5354e53 (inventory script in the Dossier): 59 shared components, but 1,325 buttons outside them with 548 distinct first classes and 20 radii, 107 locally styled tables, 26 local dialogs, fields in 142 templates with no field component, 139 font-size values, no self-hosted font (the capture host renders a CJK fallback) and an undeclared radius token used 50 times. Recommended: an Angular library project frontend/projects/studio-ui with an import boundary, own checks and a catalogue app showing every state in both themes; the 27 generic shared components moved in unchanged; families in order of need (layout and sections, buttons and menus, grid with Access moved on, self-hosted Inter, forms, overlays, states); twelve U-rules in docs/system/ui-standard/rules.md enforced per reworked page by a guard and Stylelint; the design skill and visual review read the standard; pages reworked one card at a time, daily surfaces first, with owner review between cards. Eleven decisions, sixteen slices.

openDecisions.title: Where the library lives
openDecisions.question: Where does the component library live and how is it consumed?

options.A: Angular library project frontend/projects/studio-ui in the frontend workspace, consumed through a path alias
options.B: Separate npm package in this repository (packages/studio-ui), built and versioned
options.C: Repository of its own, published and pinned like coding-agent-chat

openDecisions.rationale: Lowest cost and one-commit changes across library and page; independence comes from an import boundary, own checks and own docs. coding-agent-chat shows the price of C: pinned at 0.4.1 since 7 September 2026 with two post-install patch scripts. Move to B only if a second product consumes the library.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Angular library project frontend/projects/studio-ui in the frontend workspace, consumed through a path alias

openDecisions.title: Living catalogue
openDecisions.question: How is the catalogue of components with their states built?

options.A: Own Angular catalogue app in the workspace, states as data in *.catalogue.ts, Playwright screenshots without backend

openDecisions.rationale: Uses the existing mockup-app pattern and tooling, renders the live components, doubles as visual regression and owner review material, and its data files are readable by agents.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Own Angular catalogue app in the workspace, states as data in *.catalogue.ts, Playwright screenshots without backend

openDecisions.title: Selector prefix
openDecisions.question: What prefix do library components use?

options.A: New prefix sui- with the old app- selector kept as an alias on moved components until the last app- user is gone

openDecisions.rationale: Makes library use visible in templates and in guards, while the alias keeps every existing page and lint gate working without churn.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. New prefix sui- with the old app- selector kept as an alias on moved components until the last app- user is gone

openDecisions.title: Where the UI standard lives
openDecisions.question: Where are the UI standard rules written?

options.A: docs/system/ui-standard/rules.md (U1 to U12) beside the pilot notes, with one pointer rule R10 in style-guide-hard-rules.md

openDecisions.rationale: Keeps the hard rules short, gives the standard one file that skill, prompt and review read, and supersedes the family pages instead of adding a sixth parallel source.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. docs/system/ui-standard/rules.md (U1 to U12) beside the pilot notes, with one pointer rule R10 in style-guide-hard-rules.md

openDecisions.title: How rules are enforced
openDecisions.question: How is the standard enforced?

options.A: Per reworked page: guard check-ui-standard.mjs with an enforced list, a Stylelint override for enforced folders, the visual review aspect citing rule ids, and the design skill
options.B: Review aspect and design skill only
options.C: Global lint for the whole frontend at once

openDecisions.rationale: The families that converged (status, menus, disclosure) each had a component plus a guard with a baseline. A per-page enforced list locks each reworked page without breaking pages not yet reworked; C would fail hundreds of files on day one.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Per reworked page: guard check-ui-standard.mjs with an enforced list, a Stylelint override for enforced folders, the visual review aspect citing rule ids, and the design skill

openDecisions.title: Grid implementation
openDecisions.question: What is the data grid built on?

options.A: Own sui-data-grid on native table semantics, CDK only for focus and overlay helpers

openDecisions.rationale: The Studio's lists are tens to hundreds of rows; native table semantics give screen reader support for free, the responsive stacked form already exists on Access, and no new dependency or theme bridge is needed.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Own sui-data-grid on native table semantics, CDK only for focus and overlay helpers

openDecisions.title: Product-hosted fonts
openDecisions.question: Which font does the library ship?

options.A: Self-host Inter and JetBrains Mono (woff2 with licences, font-display swap) as the admin guideline requires, applied globally in one owner-reviewed card
options.B: Keep the system stack (Segoe UI, system-ui)
options.C: Switch the font page by page

openDecisions.rationale: The owner wants product-hosted fonts and the admin guideline already names Inter and JetBrains Mono, yet no woff2 ships; the capture host renders the Studio in a CJK fallback, so agent screenshots and reviews see another typeface than the owner. Segoe UI cannot be redistributed. C would mix fonts across pages for months.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Self-host Inter and JetBrains Mono (woff2 with licences, font-display swap) as the admin guideline requires, applied globally in one owner-reviewed card

openDecisions.title: Order of pages
openDecisions.question: In which order are pages reworked?

options.A: By use (daily, weekly, occasional) and then by local vocabulary: Board, task detail in three cards, Dossier viewer, shell chrome, Deck pages, settings pages
options.B: Settings family first (closest to the Access pilot, lowest risk), then Deck, then daily surfaces

openDecisions.rationale: The owner gains most where he spends his day; the library is proven on Access and in the catalogue before the Board. The use classes are inferred from page roles because no page-view telemetry exists; the owner confirms or edits them in rollout.md.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. By use (daily, weekly, occasional) and then by local vocabulary: Board, task detail in three cards, Dossier viewer, shell chrome, Deck pages, settings pages

openDecisions.title: Size of a page card
openDecisions.question: How large is one page card?

options.A: One page per card; task detail split into three cards along its panes; the five smallest settings pages (Updates, Appearance, Credentials, Secrets, GitHub) in one card
options.B: Strictly one page per card, including the smallest

openDecisions.rationale: Keeps each owner review to one readable set of before and after screenshots; the five smallest pages have a local vocabulary of 3 to 11 and would make five near-empty reviews.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. One page per card; task detail split into three cards along its panes; the five smallest settings pages (Updates, Appearance, Credentials, Secrets, GitHub) in one card

openDecisions.title: Existing shared components
openDecisions.question: What happens to the 59 shared components in src/app/components?

options.A: Move the 27 generic primitives into the library unchanged, with app- aliases; domain components stay in the app
options.B: Wrap them with new library components
options.C: Leave them and build new library components beside them

openDecisions.rationale: A move with no visual change gives the library its first 27 components at once, keeps all gates working, and avoids two competing versions of menu, dialog or status.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Move the 27 generic primitives into the library unchanged, with app- aliases; domain components stay in the app

openDecisions.title: Ownership and change path
openDecisions.question: Who changes the library and how?

options.A: Owner approves the standard and each new family in the catalogue; library cards own the library; page cards may add variants and small components under the library contract
options.B: Every library change is its own card
options.C: Page cards change the library freely

openDecisions.rationale: New families get their own review; small additions a page really needs land with the page under the same contract, so a page card is not blocked by a separate card for one variant.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Owner approves the standard and each new family in the catalogue; library cards own the library; page cards may add variants and small components under the library contract

# LF-1 · Library project, boundary and catalogue skeleton

Source: `docs/look-and-feel-overhaul/index.html` (AGT-4030) and its `workbench.json`. Decisions: LF-D1 (A), LF-D2 (A), LF-D3 (A). Dependencies: none.

**Area:** `frontend/angular.json`, `frontend/package.json` (scripts only), `frontend/tsconfig*.json` (path alias), `frontend/eslint.config.js`, new `frontend/projects/studio-ui/**`, new `frontend/projects/studio-ui-catalogue/**`

## Why
Dossier sections Library and Cost of checks. The frontend has 59 shared components in `src/app/components/` but no place that is developed and checked on its own; the existing mockup apps in `angular.json` show the workspace pattern.

## Deliver
1. Add an Angular library project `studio-ui` at `frontend/projects/studio-ui` with `src/public-api.ts`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and an empty `src/lib/`. Selector prefix `sui`.
2. Add a path alias `@studio/ui` to the app tsconfig so the app consumes the library source; no build or publish step, no `file:` dependency.
3. Add an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` block that fails when any file under `frontend/projects/studio-ui/` imports from `frontend/src/app/`, `coding-agent-chat` or `src/app/services`. Add a test fixture proving the rule fires.
4. Add an Angular application `studio-ui-catalogue` at `frontend/projects/studio-ui-catalogue` that discovers `*.catalogue.ts` files (states as plain data: label, inputs, content, theme, width) and renders every entry in light and dark with the component README beside it. Ship one sample entry.
5. Add `projects/studio-ui-catalogue/e2e/catalogue.spec.ts` and a Playwright config that serves the static catalogue build (no backend) and compares each entry at 1440 and 390 px in both themes against checked-in screenshots.
6. Add scripts `ui:test` (library unit tests only), `ui:lint` (ESLint and Stylelint for the two projects), `ui:catalogue` (serve), `ui:catalogue:check` (build plus screenshot spec) and `ui:api` (writes `projects/studio-ui/api-report.md` from `public-api.ts` and fails when it differs from the checked-in report).

## Acceptance
- `npm run ui:test`, `npm run ui:lint` and `npm run ui:catalogue:check` pass without the backend and without `dotnet publish`.
- An import from `src/app` inside the library fails `npm run lint` with the boundary rule.
- The app builds with the alias and `npm run lint` and `npm test` stay green; no product page changes.

## Verification
Run the four new scripts, `npm --prefix frontend run lint`, `npm --prefix frontend test`. No product Playwright run is needed because no product template changes; say so in the result.
